# Guidance improvement campaign, September 15

Authorized duration: 12:47–17:47 EDT. Two experiment GPUs in allocation 10446392.
Checkpoint: unconditional bidirectional articulated UNet, EMA, clean context;
SHA256 `99ec6cc6102a0d654c375c9f7b9cc9c86edd0964acf9de1acb42d4fb578c9fba`.

The preceding eight distinct-goal experiments improved final position but none
reached the target for the full six-frame hold. Final errors were 62–84 mm for
the bottle and 86–125 mm for the teacup. All runs saturated the noise-change cap
in their last two windows and continued improving late in their 24-update
budget. Small mesh overlap alone did not establish executable physics.

The immutable experiment plan and individual receipts are in
[the campaign directory](../../validation/guidance_push_2026-09-15/PLAN.json).
The completed [gallery guide](../../validation/guidance_push_2026-09-15/README.md) links predictions, independent execution, all outcomes and reproducibility checks.

## Comparisons

1. Hold the scene, initial draw, target, horizon and physical objective fixed.
   Compare 24/64 updates and per-window noise-change RMS caps of 0.25/0.50 on
   bottle and teacup leftward goals. Save best-so-far results through update 24
   within each 64-update run. The prior 24-update runs remain separate references.
2. Test stronger position-goal weighting independently of rotation and physical
   terms. Longer horizons add physical time and additional model windows; use
   observed context with explicit placeholder futures, never invented recordings.
3. Add supplied static obstacle geometry to planning, with full collision-body
   costs and a denser trajectory audit. The checkpoint does not receive these
   obstacles as conditioning. This is a test of avoidance through optimization.
4. Replicate useful settings on opposite targets and additional scene samples.
   Replay selected plans in the previously qualified independent MuJoCo setup
   at two timesteps. Keep model task success, geometric checks and execution
   success separate. Source-PhysX execution is still outside this campaign.
5. Publish a local Markdown gallery showing ordinary sampling, targets, guided
   paths, obstacles where applicable, and independent execution when available.
   Record failures and pending checks alongside successful-looking examples.

No training or remote push is included. Model weights remain frozen. Running
packets use immutable source snapshots and stop before the report deadline.

## Implementation checks

`--goal-weight` changes position-goal strength while retaining raw metric units
and independent rotation/contact/penetration weights. Its default is 1.
Feedback replanning carries the saved weight forward.

`--context-only-future` builds any requested rigid planning horizon from the
observed context. Particle observations are preserved bitwise; future positions
and poses repeat the anchor and future actions/targets are zero placeholders.
Saved ground-truth arrays retain only the available recording, with their length
declared in the protocol. Neither helper changes the default sampling path.

Initial validation: 60 physical-objective, collision-distance, feedback and
unconditional-guidance tests passed, including goal-gradient isolation and
poisoned-future independence of extended planning batches.

Static obstacles are supplied with `--obstacles <JSON>`, using a version-1
specification with `units: metres` and a `boxes` list. Each box has a unique
`name`, world `centre`, full `size`, and optional proper 3×3 `rotation`.
`--obstacle-weight`, `--obstacle-clearance-mm`, `--obstacle-substeps` and
`--obstacle-audit-substeps` control the objective and denser audit independently.
The initial defaults are weight 5, clearance 5 mm, three optimization probes per
transition and ten audit probes. Full convex collision components cover every
supplied moving body. Interpolated probes use per-body linear translation and
shortest rotation, not joint-space execution or exact continuous collision
detection. The audit includes the observed anchor; the optimizer cannot change it.

The MuJoCo replay accepts the same obstacle file and refuses to replay a saved
obstacle-conditioned objective while omitting its obstacle geometry. Feedback
replanning preserves that file and its costs. Obstacle augmented-Lagrangian and
specialized staged methods are explicitly rejected until separately supported.

Validation after obstacle integration: 73 guidance tests passed, followed by 15
obstacle geometry and independent-engine checks. These include clear endpoints
with an obstructed intermediate translation or rotation, finite-difference
gradients, full-body coverage and indexing, and physical contact with both the
object and gripper collision categories in MuJoCo. These are implementation
checks; experiment success remains to be established.

`--goal-reduction max` is an optional position-only cost over the held interval,
matching the worst-frame position criterion used by the task screen. Default
`mean` behavior is preserved. Rotation and physical penalties are unchanged,
and feedback carries the saved reduction forward. Tests verify the maximum and
its gradient against the independent held-position residual for picking and placing.

## First completed comparison (13:17 EDT)

For the same bottle leftward target and seed, the four paired settings give:

| Updates / noise cap | Final position error | Worst held error | Full task geometry |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| 24 / 0.25 | 71.5 mm | 86.8 mm | Fail |
| 24 / 0.50 | 37.1 mm | 66.8 mm | Fail |
| 64 / 0.25 | 61.3 mm | 78.2 mm | Fail |
| 64 / 0.50 | 4.7 mm | 31.1 mm | Fail |

The larger-cap, longer-budget run selects update 63. Its final pose is accurate,
but the six-frame hold and several contact/relative-motion checks still fail.
Both independent physics replays fail to lift the bottle and disagree with
each other after contact. This is improved model goal reaching, not an executed
pick success. All eight preceding distinct-goal plans also fail their complete
execution tests. Failed constraints and all measurements are retained.

The subsequent completed experiments compare 68-frame futures, stronger
position-goal weight, obstacle costs, worst-frame goals, stronger interaction
penalties and actuator-only noise updates; results follow below.

## Research context for the physical checks

Close fingers are only a geometric prerequisite. Contact directions, friction,
force/torque balance and the resulting dynamics also matter; MIT's
[grasping notes](https://manipulation.csail.mit.edu/clutter.html) discuss these
distinctions and antipodal grasp heuristics. The current costs do not solve a
force-balance problem. A normals-based diagnostic may help investigate failures,
but an unqualified force-closure approximation should not become an acceptance test.

The [PROWL study](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.18803) reports exploitation of
diffusion world models under weak behavior constraints in a different domain.
That motivates testing trust bounds and validating generated plans independently;
it does not establish the cause of this model's failures or justify a universal
noise cap. This campaign keeps the checkpoint frozen and tests that question
empirically.

## Replay and contact investigation (14:20 EDT)

The teacup at 64 updates/cap 0.50 reaches 1.6 mm and passes the model's full
geometry screen. Its independent replays still finish 85.6/88.6 mm from the
target and fail task and timestep checks. Predicted geometry alone is insufficient.

A concrete replay-adapter artifact was reproduced: toggling the original
proximity-triggered 6 mm preload can turn a 0.3 mm predicted closing motion into
a 5.7 mm opening command. The optional `--preload-policy latched` retains closure
through proximity flicker, releases after a 2 mm mean opening stroke, and rearms
after a new closing stroke. Original `instant` behavior remains bitwise unchanged.
Feedback rejects the latched option until its state can be carried across replans.

This is not a demonstrated repair of task execution. Requalification on all 16
recorded controls gives 10 qualified controls versus 11 for the original policy;
none of the four fixed generated plans passes under the latched policy. The
complete audit is in `validation/guidance_push_2026-09-15/PRELOAD_DIAGNOSTIC.md`.

Solver-step force audits replay saved integration states bitwise and verify force
frame/sign conversion against MuJoCo's passive-body constraint force. For the
bottle's 64-update/cap-0.50 plan, both fingers exert positive normal force for
0.18% of the rollout, versus 35.72% for its recorded control. These are independent
engine measurements, not calibrated source-simulator or robot forces. Every new
execution gallery entry now includes this denser contact/penetration audit.

A further diagnostic fixes the generated gripper path through actuator inpainting
and resamples only valid passive-object noise channels. It checks the original
sample's exact replay first, then verifies actuator poses and deltas remain fixed
across windows. The inpainted reference itself can change the intermediate
denoising states; this is a consistency probe, not an exact conditional distribution.

An exploratory gravity-support check uses FCL witness contacts and inscribed
friction cones in a force/torque-balance linear program. Four synthetic tests
cover opposing contacts, unilateral forces, friction, moment balance, normal
force limits and soft-finger torsion. It is not used for acceptance or guidance:
the point-contact version rejects all nine elevated frames of the successful
recorded bottle control. Adding the replay's declared 0.005 m torsional friction
admits seven of nine recorded frames and ten of fourteen generated frames.
Thus this simplified static check neither qualifies the control fully nor
explains the dynamic execution failure. Contact patch structure, compression and
time evolution still matter. The coupled soft-finger cone follows the
[MuJoCo contact definition](https://mujoco.readthedocs.io/en/stable/computation/index.html#friction-cones).
Reports are retained under `support_probe_*` and `support_soft_probe_*` in the
campaign directory, including the unsuccessful diagnostic.

## Ordinary-sample controls and physical-cost ablation (14:50 EDT)

The exact unguided samples for the bottle/teacup seed also fail replay. Their
full model geometry screens fail before guidance: bottle peak overlap is
5.54 mm; teacup peak overlap is 2.72 mm and its resting/release checks fail.
The optimization comparisons therefore do not establish that guidance created
all physical failures.

An additional CPU audit replays every retained draw in the old 16-sample can and
spice-jar banks. Checkpoint hash and the corrected 16+16+4 window contract match
this campaign; every original generation receipt and draw hash is retained.
Two of 32 pass the declared replay-fidelity criterion, both spice-jar draws.
Draw 10 lifts 358.4 mm and stays within 4.3 mm of its predicted final position at
both timesteps. This criterion tests lifting and prediction fidelity, not arrival
at an external new goal. All 32 model trajectories fail at least one strict
non-goal geometry check, including the two that execute successfully. Thus those
screens can also reject useful but geometrically imperfect model predictions.
These previously inspected fixtures are not a population estimate or a held-out
model evaluation. The four new lateral replication targets were already frozen
before this bank audit and retain a separate fixed seed, 9351.

`--physical-weight` scales the weighted physical penalties as one group while
preserving position and rotation goals, noise regularization, and separately
supplied obstacle costs. Its default 1 preserves the original numerical loss;
0 is a diagnostic ablation, not a recommended planner setting. Feedback carries
the setting forward. Validation: 59 core/physical/feedback tests and 14 obstacle
tests passed; real bottle and teacup fixture probes verify the zero-physics loss
and zero direct gripper/particle gradients while preserving the task goal.
Matched 24-update, cap-0.50 experiments will measure its effect against the saved
physical-objective prefixes. All geometry and execution checks remain active in
reporting, regardless of the optimization weights.

## Obstacle and window diagnostics (15:25 EDT)

The two initial obstacle runs avoid the barrier in their predicted paths but
stop short: bottle minimum clearance 5.22 mm / final error 113.3 mm; teacup
5.42 mm / 170.1 mm. The teacup's independent replays have zero barrier contacts
but finish 180.7/180.5 mm from the target. The bottle's failed grasp leads to
17/33 solver steps with barrier contact despite its clear predicted path.
The [four-panel surface comparison](../../validation/guidance_push_2026-09-15/OBSTACLE_GALLERY.md)
uses the same barrier in both reference and avoidance replays. The reference
is its original frozen plan, not a second optimization in the obstacle world.

The [window diagnostics](../../validation/guidance_push_2026-09-15/WINDOW_DIAGNOSTICS.md)
plot per-window noise-budget use and total-objective gradient RMS, accounting
for the shorter final window. They show continued gradients and saturated
late-window noise bounds in the 36-frame bottle runs. The 68-frame run improves
predicted held-position reaching without exhausting its cap, yet still fails
independent execution. More horizon and more noise freedom address predicted
reaching; they have not repaired the grasp dynamics.

Four replication targets were frozen at 14:24 EDT: left/right spice-jar picks
and left/right bowl placements, seed 9351. A later frozen rule chooses one
common method from the five 64-update development arms, ranking paired execution
passes, then full model-geometry passes, then mean worst-held position error.
No replication result can change that choice. Both fixtures were previously
inspected; these are exploratory new-goal tests, not held-out model evaluation.

The [saved-noise audit](../../validation/guidance_push_2026-09-15/LATENT_NOISE_AUDIT.md)
finds that the 64-update, cap-0.50 bottle/teacup runs change mean squared valid
pose noise from 0.973 to 1.162/1.230, and within-window adjacent-frame products
from 0.016 to 0.149/0.187. This measures changes beyond the existing distance
bound; it neither proves physical invalidity nor identifies the cause of failed
execution. A [follow-up note](CONSISTENCY_NEXT_STEPS.md) relates the remaining
consistency questions to DNO, Diffusion Forcing and action-consistency planning,
with explicit caveats for this bidirectional, jointly generated representation.

## Worst-frame goals and stronger interaction costs (16:05 EDT)

With the 36-frame horizon, cap 0.50 and 64 updates unchanged, the worst-held
position objective gives bottle/teacup held errors of 21.03/1.75 mm. The teacup
passes the model geometry screen but its replay still ends 86.1/81.0 mm from
the target. The bottle still fails contact and held-position checks.

Increasing contact/rise/slip weights from 2/5/1 to 10/50/5 with that same
worst-frame objective gives 60.05/1.20 mm held errors. The teacup again passes
model geometry and again fails execution, ending 79.3/78.0 mm away. The bottle
passes its sampled proximity check but slightly exceeds the 2 mm overlap
tolerance and misses the target. Its independent replays also fail to lift it.

The stronger bottle plan keeps the preload gate active continuously from frame
21 through frame 36, whereas the original generated plan toggles it. Nevertheless,
both-finger positive contact force occurs for only 4.32% of the fine-step replay,
compared with 0.18% for the original generated plan and 35.72% for the recorded
control. The [three-column contact plot](../../validation/guidance_push_2026-09-15/figures/grasp_replay_diagnostic.png)
and [command audit](../../validation/guidance_push_2026-09-15/strong_interaction_contact_check.json)
show that removing gate flicker is insufficient for this interaction. Proximity
and small overlap alone have not supplied a maintained physical grasp.

## Fixed-gripper consistency and new-goal replication (16:38 EDT)

All four fixed-gripper probes passed exact original-sample replay, preserved
valid actuator deltas exactly, and preserved actuator poses across windows.
The first attempt exposed a CPU/GPU mask mismatch before any resampling; commit
`80a7c15` corrects the diagnostic, and the failed receipt remains alongside the
fresh `_v11` reruns. The model and optimizer were unaffected by that correction.

| Plan | Original worst held error | Inpainted reference | Eight fresh passive-noise draws |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Bottle, all-pose noise / mean goal | 31.1 mm | 24.0 mm | 65.2–114.8 mm |
| Bottle, actuator noise / worst-frame goal | 78.1 mm | 72.3 mm | 83.2–100.1 mm |
| Teacup, all-pose noise / mean goal | 1.6 mm | 38.1 mm | 97.2–126.7 mm |
| Teacup, actuator noise / worst-frame goal | 121.2 mm | 109.4 mm | 115.1–138.8 mm |

None of these 32 fresh draws reaches the 20 mm held-position tolerance. These
are four sets of eight fixed seeds, not independent population trials. The
inpainted reference itself changes the denoising process; this is internal
model consistency, not exact conditional sampling or physics validation.
The two optimization scopes also use different goal reductions. See
[all draws and checks](../../validation/guidance_push_2026-09-15/FIXED_GRIPPER.md)
and [four-panel surface movies](../../validation/guidance_push_2026-09-15/FIXED_GRIPPER_SURFACES.md).

The frozen replication rule selected the worst-held-position objective with
default physical penalties. None of its five development arms passed complete
execution, so the rule was resolved by model geometry and held-position error;
this is not evidence of a physically validated best method. All four frozen
jar/bowl left/right targets use that same choice, seed 9351, 64 updates and
cap 0.50. Their outcomes cannot change the method selection.

The optional obstacle selection/refinement packets started after **all four**
replicas, at 21:25 UTC, within the original 21:28 UTC launch cutoff. Both
finished by 21:36 UTC. They select from 16 fully generated candidates before
24 refinement updates; they use no prescribed grasp proposal and are not
matched compute to a 64-update single-start optimization.

The completed [24-update physical-cost
ablation](../../validation/guidance_push_2026-09-15/PHYSICAL_ABLATION.md) improves
model held errors when penalties are disabled: bottle 66.8 to 46.2 mm, teacup
89.9 to 60.9 mm. The bottle then lifts in the prediction while the two fingers
never both come within 2 mm; physics leaves it on the table. Teacup peak mesh overlap
increases from 1.53 to 6.09 mm, and its zero-penalty prediction intrudes below
the table by 10.57 mm. All four complete execution tests fail. Physical costs
improve some geometric behavior but do not establish a maintained grasp.

A post-hoc [transport proximity
check](../../validation/guidance_push_2026-09-15/TRANSPORT_PROXIMITY.md) also fails
to explain the main replay gap through large visible separation. At a 5 mm
finger-distance threshold, every tested development plan using physical costs
has zero flagged airborne lateral travel. Stronger-interaction plans have zero
even at 2 mm. These threshold probes leave the frozen acceptance criteria
unchanged and do not treat proximity or overlap as proof of contact force.

## Execution timing and preload follow-up (17:12 EDT)

A separate CPU [timing diagnostic](../../validation/guidance_push_2026-09-15/TIMING_PROBE.md)
reuses five fixed generated gripper command paths and three recorded controls
at both solver steps. All 16 original-speed pose/joint replays match bitwise
before changing timing. Doubling command duration from 1.8 to 3.6 seconds leaves
every generated plan outside the 20 mm held-position tolerance. The recorded
controls' endpoint errors remain 1.9–11.4 mm at the slower speed. These retimed
executions are not new predictions from the learned model; the physical initial
velocities stay fixed and the held interval also doubles. Slower execution alone
does not repair these plans.

The new leftward jar plan reveals another instance of the preload-gate artifact:
at its peak-height frame 26, the gate turns off and introduces about 6 mm of
finger opening. The already implemented latched policy preserves closure and
keeps the object lifted through the end. Final position error improves from
174.7/178.7 mm to 32.5/35.2 mm at the two timesteps. It still fails held-position,
penetration and timestep-agreement criteria, so this is a partial controller
improvement, not a completed pick. A separate [four-target controller
comparison](../../validation/guidance_push_2026-09-15/LATCHED_REPLICATION.md)
uses the existing 16-control qualification and fixed thresholds. It leaves the
original-policy primary comparisons and replication method selection unchanged.

## Four new-goal outcomes (17:29 EDT)

All four frozen replicas completed with one common setting and seed 9351.
Three reach the 20 mm held-position tolerance in the model; only the rightward
bowl passes the full model geometry screen. None passes complete independent
execution with either tested preload policy.

| Goal | Model worst held error | Original replay, worse timestep | Latched replay, worse timestep |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Jar left | 10.1 mm | 178.7 mm | 38.5 mm |
| Jar right | 71.3 mm | 166.5 mm | 70.7 mm |
| Bowl left | 18.2 mm | 137.9 mm | 55.5 mm |
| Bowl right | 3.6 mm | 65.2 mm | 114.5 mm |

The latched rightward jar passes every declared **non-goal** execution check:
control qualification, contact/penetration, tracking, relative motion and
timestep agreement. Its remaining failure is the requested destination.
Latched preload improves three endpoint errors but worsens the rightward bowl;
it remains optional. See [all four outcomes and opposite-goal
movies](../../validation/guidance_push_2026-09-15/REPLICATION.md).

A bounded [representative-point randomness
probe](../../validation/guidance_push_2026-09-15/ROUTING_PROBE.md) used otherwise
idle GPU time after the jar runs. The optimized Gaussian arrays stay fixed;
four fresh per-window routing seeds change the leftward jar's object path by
0.54–1.70 mm, with held errors 9.81–10.68 mm. Original particle coordinates
reproduce exactly under the saved routing. This one-draw check does not find
large path sensitivity and does not establish dataset-wide or physical robustness.

## Final obstacle selection and delivery

Both 16-candidate/24-update runs completed. Weighted selection chose bottle
candidate 8 and teacup candidate 13; the report retains every candidate, rather
than just the selected trajectory. Selected refinement iterates are 19 and 22.

| Scene | Model worst held error | Ten-probe minimum clearance | Replay worst held error |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Bottle | 162.9 mm | 4.88 mm | 203.7 mm |
| Teacup | 169.1 mm | 5.19 mm | 177.0 mm |

Neither solves its task. The bottle narrowly misses the declared 5 mm model
clearance; both physical replays avoid barrier contact but remain far from the
goal. The teacup also exceeds the 2 mm dense object–gripper overlap threshold
at the coarser timestep (2.69 mm). Both pairs fail timestep agreement. Selecting
more starting draws has not repaired obstacle goal reaching in this budget.
See [all candidates](../../validation/guidance_push_2026-09-15/OBSTACLE_CANDIDATES.md)
and the final entries in the [surface gallery](../../validation/guidance_push_2026-09-15/SURFACE_GALLERY.md).

All planned GPU experiments have completed. Exact initial-sample pairing passes
for 18 comparisons across six cohorts, including candidate zero in selection
runs. The primary gallery contains 34 entries including shared prefixes and
controls, not independent trials. The timing diagnostic additionally reproduces
all 16 nominal instrumented executions bitwise. Source snapshots, hashes,
optimization traces, all candidates, replay states and force audits are retained
in the campaign directory. Implementation and reports are committed locally;
large validation artifacts remain local and ignored by Git.

The strongest next step is to test guidance that remains successful under fresh
passive-object noise and improve the mapping from generated achieved poses to
executable gripper commands. More iterations alone improved predicted goals but
did not close the execution gap. The [follow-up design](CONSISTENCY_NEXT_STEPS.md)
separates those hypotheses and their required controls. No result here validates
source-PhysX or hardware execution, and the small inspected fixture set is not a
population success estimate.

Final delivery checks verified 518 local links across 23 report pages, all 34
exported trajectory hashes and 68 exact force replays. All 78 referenced GIFs
decode fully. Both allocated experiment GPUs are idle.
